papers.title: A Graph-Based Machine Learning Framework to Assign Empirical Interaction Parameters for Novel Molecules.
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of novel molecules are essential to modern drug discovery and related fields that require large-scale sampling of chemical space. However, obtaining accurate and robust force field parameters for novel molecules remains a major challenge. One approach to this problem is to perform quantum chemical calculations on a per-molecule basis, but doing so on a large scale is prohibitively expensive. Here, we present a graph-based machine learning framework for empirical force field assignment that scales significantly more efficiently with molecule size than quantum
papers.summary: The authors present a graph-based machine learning framework that assigns empirical force field parameters to novel molecules, avoiding costly per-molecule quantum chemical calculations. This approach scales more efficiently with molecular size, potentially enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations for drug discovery.

papers.title: From Phenotypic Screening to Target and Compound Prioritization for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is a progressive kidney disorder with limited therapeutic options, highlighting an urgent need for safer, long-term treatments. This study presents a multi-step computational and experimental approach to identify and assess target-based hypotheses for mechanisms underlying the cAMP-dependent cyst swelling. We analyzed phenotypic screening data from a 3D mIMCD3-Pkd1-/- forskolin-induced, cAMP-driven cyst swelling (CS) assay, classifying compounds based on their CS activity. These compounds were cross-referenced with the Papyrus database to id
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study combines phenotypic screening data from a 3D ADPKD cyst-swelling assay with computational cross-referencing against the Papyrus bioactivity database to identify and prioritize drug targets and compounds for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. The workflow moves from phenotypic hits to target-based hypotheses, offering a framework for rational therapeutic development in a disease with limited treatment options.

papers.title: Elucidating the beneficial effects of gut microbiota-derived metabolites in treating hepatocellular carcinoma: an integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing analysis.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While accumulating evidence has highlighted the beneficial effects of gut microbiota (GM)-derived metabolites in HCC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We retrieved GM-derived metabolites from gutMGene v2.0, acquired their targets using the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) and Swiss Target Prediction (STP), and identified HCC-related targets from public databases. Overlapping targets were then obtained via Venn diagram analysis. We constr
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing to investigate how gut microbiota-derived metabolites may help treat hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The authors identified overlapping targets between microbiota metabolite targets and HCC-related genes, then used docking and single-cell data to prioritize mechanisms and cell types involved. The work provides a computational framework for understanding microbiota-metabolite-host interactions in liver cancer.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational systems-biology method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize drug combinations that could overcome primary non-response to targeted therapies. By analyzing how individual drugs shift patient transcriptomic signatures over time, the approach narrows the vast space of possible drug pairs to the most promising candidates for combination therapy.

papers.title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing has emerged as an attractive strategy in contemporary pharmaceutical research, presenting an opportunity to expedite drug discovery, minimize developmental costs, and mitigate risks associated with developing new pharmaceuticals. In this study, we investigated a novel approach based on deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms for systematic identification of additional therapeutic potential in preexisting drugs. We trained a composite feedforward neural network model using gene expression data sourced from the ARCHS4 compilation of the GEO, encompassing extensive human
papers.summary: The authors trained a feedforward neural network on human gene expression data from ARCHS4 to predict drug mechanisms and identify repurposing candidates, applying it to cardiac hypertrophy as a case study. The model highlights how deep learning on transcriptomic data can systematically uncover new therapeutic uses for existing drugs.

papers.title: Global Research Trends and Insights on AI Usage in Tuberculosis: Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge despite prevention efforts. AI offers promising approaches to long-standing challenges in TB diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management; however, a systematic mapping of global research priorities and translational gaps in AI applications to TB is currently lacking.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis systematically maps global research trends and priorities in AI applications for tuberculosis, covering areas such as diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management. It identifies key research hotspots, leading contributors, and translational gaps, providing a comprehensive overview of where the field is heading and where more work is needed.

papers.title: From QSAR to deep learning: an interpretable comprehensive pipeline with a read-across approach for mutagenicity prediction via the Enalos Cloud Platform.
papers.abstract: Assessing the mutagenicity of chemical compounds is essential for ensuring their safe handling and use, thereby minimizing potential health risks. New approach methodologies (NAMs), including computational approaches, provide non-animal alternatives for testing novel materials and chemicals. This study highlights the potential of in silico NAMs, which can contribute to the development of novel Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and substances by identifying potentially hazardous ones at an early stage. Emphasis is given to the mutagenicity prediction based on data from the Ames (b
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling, deep learning, and a read-across approach to predict chemical mutagenicity, deployed via the Enalos Cloud Platform. The tool aims to support non-animal safety assessment and early-stage identification of hazardous compounds in the context of Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemical development.

papers.title: Decision-grade evidence for AI-enabled small-molecule discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now guides choices across small-molecule discovery, yet benchmark gains rarely reveal whether a model changed the next compound, assay or project decision. This Perspective organizes public evidence around Design, Make, Test and Analyze (DMTA) handoffs. It distinguishes reproducible benchmark evidence (C1), use-relevant retrospective robustness (C2), executed Make or Test handoffs (C3), prospective workflow comparisons (C4-W) and traceable downstream trajectories (C4-D), with separate Evaluation, Deliverability and Governance profiles. Two authors independently screened
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This perspective proposes a framework for evaluating AI in small-molecule discovery based on whether models actually change real project decisions, rather than just benchmark performance. It defines evidence tiers (C1-C4) spanning reproducible benchmarks, retrospective robustness, executed Make/Test handoffs, and prospective workflow comparisons, with separate Evaluation, Deliverability, and Governance profiles.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational evaluation of atractylenolide III from Tubipora musica for anticancer lead identification.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health challenge, with over 900,000 new cases annually and a pronounced male predominance. In pursuit of novel, low-toxicity therapeutics, this study isolated Atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and demonstrated measurable, dose-dependent cytotoxic activity against HepG2 liver cancer cells, achieving an IC50 value of 15.50 µg/mL and reducing cell viability to 25.0% at 25 µg/mL. To investigate potential molecular targets and propose hypothetical mechanism pathways, we employed a multi-layered computational strategy. Mol
papers.summary: This study isolated atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and showed it kills HepG2 liver cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner (IC50 = 15.50 µg/mL). Computational docking and network analyses were then used to propose hypothetical molecular targets and mechanisms underlying this anticancer activity.

papers.title: An interpretable framework applying protein words to predict protein-small molecule complementary pairing rules.
papers.abstract: Despite the high accuracy of 'black box' deep learning models, drug discovery still relies on protein-ligand interaction principles and heuristics. To improve interpretability of protein-small molecule binding predictions, we developed the PWRules framework, which applies binding affinity data to identify privileged small molecule fragments and subsequently defines complementary pairing rules between these fragments and protein words (semantic sequence units) through an interpretability module. The resulting word-fragment rules are then used by the PWScore function to prioritize active compoun
papers.summary: The authors present PWRules, an interpretable framework that learns 'protein words' (semantic sequence units) and pairs them with privileged small-molecule fragments using binding affinity data. A scoring function, PWScore, then uses these word-fragment rules to prioritize active compounds, offering a more interpretable alternative to black-box deep learning models for protein-ligand binding prediction.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction of Dose-Linear Pharmacokinetics: Utilizing Molecular Descriptors to Guide Formulation Strategy.
papers.abstract: Early stage preclinical drug formulation development can be impacted by limited materials and time, especially when making rapid, data-driven decisions is critical. An important parameter to consider is dose linearity, as this can guide the selection between determining if a conventional or enabled formulation strategy is necessary to achieve the expected target exposure as the dose is escalated. This work explores the application of machine learning models to predict dose linearity for compounds administered to the mouse species based on the molecular properties. We utilize a diverse set of m
papers.summary: This study applies machine learning models to predict whether drug compounds will exhibit dose-linear pharmacokinetics in mice, using molecular descriptors as inputs. The goal is to help formulation scientists decide early in preclinical development whether a conventional or enabling formulation strategy is needed, saving time and material. The approach demonstrates that molecular properties can guide data-driven formulation decisions.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and realistic cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the determinants of success differ between the two classes of methods, with AI approaches excelling in some regimes while physics-based tools retain advantages in others. The work highlights that cross-docking remains a substantially harder test than redocking and that no single method dominates across all scenarios.

papers.title: Deep learning-based structural prediction (AlphaFold 3) of shrimp IMNV RdRp and identification of seaweed-derived metabolites for antiviral intervention in aquaculture.
papers.abstract: Infectious Myonecrosis Virus (IMNV) remains a major global threat to shrimp aquaculture, causing severe economic losses due to the lack of approved antiviral therapeutics. In this study, an advanced in silico approach was employed, utilizing a deep learning-based prediction of AlphaFold 3 protein structures and large-scale virtual screening of seaweed-derived metabolites to identify potential inhibitors targeting RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). To identify potential seaweed-derived candidate compounds against IMNV, a total of 1077 compounds were screened against the RdRp_M01 protein. The
papers.summary: This study used AlphaFold 3 to predict the structure of the shrimp IMNV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and virtually screened 1,077 seaweed-derived metabolites against it to find potential antiviral compounds. The work demonstrates a computational pipeline combining deep learning-based structure prediction with natural product screening to address a disease threatening global shrimp aquaculture.

papers.title: XenoSoM: A deep learning framework for site of metabolism prediction of xenobiotics.
papers.abstract: Metabolic biotransformations significantly influence drug efficacy and safety, making early metabolism assessment crucial in drug discovery. While in vivo and in vitro methods remain the gold standard for investigating metabolic properties, they are often costly and time-consuming. Consequently, AI-driven models have emerged as useful tools to predict metabolic reactions, sites of metabolism (SoM), and resulting metabolites. Predicting the SoM is particularly valuable for identifying reactive atoms and anticipating compounds' metabolic profile. In this study, six deep learning architectures (G
papers.summary: XenoSoM is a deep learning framework designed to predict the site of metabolism (SoM) of xenobiotics, addressing a key challenge in early drug discovery where experimental methods are costly and slow. The authors evaluated six deep learning architectures to identify reactive atoms and anticipate metabolic profiles of compounds. This tool aims to support medicinal chemists in assessing drug metabolism computationally.

papers.title: Revisiting the LSER Approach in the Era of Machine Learning: Insights from IAM Chromatography.
papers.abstract: The present study demonstrates the integration of the linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) concept with machine learning (ML) methodologies to improve the predictive and interpretative capabilities of chromatographic retention modeling. Immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was employed as a model biochromatographic system, and an in-house library of 993 structurally diverse compounds, with experimentally determined chromatographic hydrophobicity index of IAM (CHIIAM), was used to train LSER-ML models. LSER descriptors were calculated using Absolv and extended with ioniza
papers.summary: This study combines the classical linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) framework with machine learning to model chromatographic retention on immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) columns. Using a library of 993 structurally diverse compounds with measured CHIIAM values, the authors show that LSER descriptors augmented with ionization information can improve both prediction and interpretation of retention behavior. The work demonstrates how traditional physicochemical modeling concepts can be enhanced by ML in the era of data-driven chemistry.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for oligopeptide candidate discovery across metabolism-related contexts.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods are increasingly critical in therapeutic peptide discovery but have been concentrated in certain applications, such as the development of antimicrobial peptides. Therapeutic peptide discovery in contexts such as metabolism, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration remains challenging due to a paucity of available indication-specific training data. Here, we propose a deep learning-based pipeline, Deepeptide, capable of identifying candidate oligopeptides for various metabolism-related contexts. Leveraging the intrinsic relationships between disease indic
papers.summary: The authors present Deepeptide, a deep learning pipeline designed to discover therapeutic oligopeptides for metabolism-related conditions such as metabolic disorders, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration, where training data are scarce. By leveraging intrinsic relationships between disease indications, the framework enables candidate peptide identification across multiple contexts without requiring large indication-specific datasets.

papers.title: Integrated Pharmacogenomic and Structure-Guided Analyses Link LCC-10 (NSC765599) to an MMP-Associated Extracellular Matrix Regulatory Network in Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Leukemia progression is increasingly shaped by reciprocal interactions between leukemic cells and the bone marrow microenvironment, yet the extracellular regulatory networks associated with these interactions remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the biological context associated with the antileukemic activity of LCC-10 (NSC765599), a synthetic biphenyl benzamide derivative, using an integrated pharmacogenomic and structure-guided computational framework. Antiproliferative activity was first characterized using the NCI-60 screen and subsequently integrated with pharmacogenomic
papers.summary: This study integrates pharmacogenomic profiling of the NCI-60 cell line panel with structure-guided computational analysis to characterize the antileukemic compound LCC-10 (NSC765599). The authors link its activity to an MMP-associated extracellular matrix regulatory network in leukemia, suggesting a role for the bone marrow microenvironment in drug response.

papers.title: Bioactive compounds from marine algae targeting MMP-9: A computational approach to rheumatoid arthritis treatment.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune systemic inflammatory condition that significantly damages bone and cartilage, leading to severe joint deformities. Matrix metalloproteinase(s) (MMP-9) plays a significant role in both the pathogenesis and management of RA, and its status as a biomarker and a target for inhibition is important in understanding and treating the disease. This work aims to examine the interactions between the molecules of MMP-9 and bioactive compounds derived from marine algae using molecular docking and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicit
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and ADMET predictions to screen bioactive compounds from marine algae as potential inhibitors of MMP-9, a matrix metalloproteinase implicated in the joint destruction seen in rheumatoid arthritis. The computational approach identifies candidate compounds that bind MMP-9 with favorable drug-like properties, suggesting marine algae as a source for anti-RA therapeutics. Findings are preliminary and would require experimental validation.

papers.title: From chemical space to synthetic reality: A framework for makeable-by-design generative AI in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular design, but many outputs are still judged by proxy metrics that do not establish whether proposed compounds can be synthesized, tested and advanced. This review reframes the field around 'synthetic reality': the extent to which AI-generated molecules survive route planning, precursor availability, experimental execution and medicinal chemistry decision-making. We examine the limits of heuristic synthesizability metrics, assess route-aware and execution-facing systems and propose maturity levels, reporting standards, actionability m
papers.summary: This review argues that generative AI in drug discovery should be evaluated by whether proposed molecules can actually be synthesized and advanced, rather than by proxy metrics like heuristic synthesizability scores. It examines the limits of current metrics, reviews route-aware and execution-facing systems, and proposes maturity levels and reporting standards for 'makeable-by-design' generative AI.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and ultra-high performance computing methods and experiments for drug discovery: virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, ADMET modelling, and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed considerable progress in computer-aided drug discovery, driven by the incorporation of computational technologies within both academic and pharmaceutical environments. This evolution is marked by a significant accumulation of data pertaining to detailed three-dimensional structural information, ligand properties, and their interactions with therapeutic targets. The augmentation of computational capabilities and the accessibility of extensive chemical libraries containing billions of drug-like small molecules have further facilitated this transition. To effectively u
papers.summary: This review surveys the integration of artificial intelligence and ultra-high performance computing across the drug discovery pipeline, covering virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET modeling. It emphasizes how massive structural and chemical datasets combined with billion-compound libraries are reshaping computational drug discovery, and highlights the role of experimental validation in closing the loop.

papers.title: Stable simulations do not guarantee functional engagement: a case study of off-target prediction for Seladelpar and Zanamivir.
papers.abstract: Identifying off-target interactions of approved drugs is important to anticipate side effects and uncover repurposing opportunities. Computational pipelines combining structural homology, structure prediction, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations offer a promising strategy, but it remains unclear whether stable, control-like MD trajectories reliably indicate functional engagement. We examined this in a case study of two approved drugs. Using the Evolutionary Classification of Protein Domains (ECOD) framework to select candidate off-targets, we modeled each drug-protein complex as two indepe
papers.summary: This study tests whether stable molecular dynamics simulations reliably indicate true off-target drug binding, using Seladelpar and Zanamivir as case studies. The authors find that stable, control-like MD trajectories do not guarantee functional engagement, cautioning against over-reliance on simulation stability as evidence for off-target interactions.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with Emerging Pharmaceutical Technologies: Current Progress, Clinical Translation, and Future Challenges.
papers.abstract: Modern scientific and technological developments are driving major advances in drug research and development. This narrative review, based on a structured search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2018-2026), examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are accelerating a historically prolonged and expensive process, alongside pharmacogenomics, organ-on-a-chip systems, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, and nanotechnology. In benchmark studies, deep learning techniques have achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of over 0.85 for a
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how AI and machine learning are being integrated with emerging pharmaceutical technologies—including pharmacogenomics, organ-on-a-chip systems, 3D bioprinting, and nanotechnology—to accelerate drug research and development. It highlights benchmark performance (e.g., deep learning AUROC above 0.85) alongside clinical translation progress and remaining challenges.

papers.title: From diligence to verification: the emergence of the TechBio-Investor.
papers.abstract: Recent technical advances, including AI co-scientists and agentic systems, increasingly allow TechBios to undertake scientific verification at scale. In addition to facilitating internal discovery efforts, these capabilities can also be used for making external investment decisions. The emerging synergies between discovery and investment enable a new type of hybrid entity, the TechBio-Investor, which has the potential to reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing. Scaled verification can help improve capital allocation, steering investment toward stronger science and, in a sector wh
papers.summary: The paper describes the emergence of a new hybrid entity, the TechBio-Investor, which leverages AI co-scientists and agentic systems to perform scientific verification at scale both for internal drug discovery and for external investment decisions. This convergence of discovery and investment capabilities could reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing by improving capital allocation toward stronger science.

papers.title: Task-adaptive multimodal molecular representations for structure-sensitive property prediction.
papers.abstract: Structure-sensitive properties (SSPs), including activity cliffs and chirality-dependent properties, challenge molecular machine learning because small structural perturbations can cause abrupt property changes and invalidate smooth structure-property assumptions. Here, we present CAMF (Chirality- and Activity-cliff-aware Multimodal Framework), a task-adaptive framework that models SSPs through selective integration of complementary molecular evidence. To systematically evaluate this problem, we construct SSPBench, a benchmark spanning 77 conventional ADMET and physicochemical tasks together w
papers.summary: The paper introduces CAMF, a task-adaptive multimodal framework that selectively integrates complementary molecular representations to better predict structure-sensitive properties such as activity cliffs and chirality-dependent effects. It also presents SSPBench, a benchmark of 77 ADMET and physicochemical tasks plus structure-sensitive tasks, to systematically evaluate models on these challenging predictions. The work highlights that standard smooth structure-property assumptions fail for such properties and shows that adaptive multimodal integration improves performance.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered High-Content Analysis: Methodologies and Applications in Bioactive Compound Discovery from Natural Sources.
papers.abstract: High-content screening (HCS) is a useful phenotypic drug discovery technology that combines automated microscopy, image analysis, and high-throughput experimentation to comprehensively characterize biological responses to diverse perturbations. This review summarizes the methodological fundamentals of high-content analysis, including image preprocessing, cell segmentation, feature processing, and downstream analysis, as well as the diverse phenotypic datasets generated from different biological models, perturbation strategies, and staining approaches. Recent advances in artificial intelligence
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being integrated into high-content screening (HCS) pipelines—covering image preprocessing, cell segmentation, feature extraction, and downstream phenotypic analysis—to discover bioactive compounds from natural sources. It catalogs the phenotypic datasets generated by different biological models, perturbation strategies, and staining approaches, and highlights recent AI-driven advances in the field.

papers.title: Heat Shock Proteins in Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Targeting.
papers.abstract: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are molecular chaperones that couple proteostasis to cancer metabolic reprogramming under oncogenic and microenvironmental stress. This Review integrates structural, biochemical, preclinical, and clinical evidence on HSP90, HSP70, HSP60, HSP40, HSP110, and small HSPs. We explain how ATPase cycles, chaperonin cages, co-chaperone networks, and organelle-specific localization stabilize metabolic enzymes, glucose transporters, hypoxia-responsive factors, and electron-transport-chain components, thereby coordinating glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox homeostas
papers.summary: This review synthesizes structural, biochemical, preclinical, and clinical evidence on how heat shock proteins (HSP90, HSP70, HSP60, HSP40, HSP110, and small HSPs) act as molecular chaperones that link protein homeostasis to metabolic reprogramming in cancer. It details how ATPase cycles, chaperonin cages, co-chaperone networks, and organelle-specific localization stabilize metabolic enzymes, glucose transporters, hypoxia-responsive factors, and electron transport chain components, thereby coordinating glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and redox homeostasis. The review also discusses therapeutic strategies for targeting HSPs in cancer.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins. It uses chemical and protein large language models to generate feature representations, then applies dual hypergraph convolutional networks built from K-nearest-neighbor graphs to capture higher-order relationships. The approach aims to expand the computational toolkit for metabolite-protein interaction prediction, with relevance to systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: MSF-HierGNN: a multi-source substructure-fusion hierarchical GNN method and web server to predict molecular property for drug design.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the biological and physicochemical properties of molecules is of great significance in shortening the process and decreasing the failure rate of drug design. Thus, previous studies have established several benchmark datasets and developed several Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) based artificial intelligence (AI) predictive methods. However, since these methods encounter challenges such as incomplete representation of molecular hierarchical structures, insufficient exploration of local topological features, and under-extraction of correlations among atomic features, our stud
papers.summary: MSF-HierGNN introduces a hierarchical graph neural network that fuses multi-source substructure information to better capture molecular hierarchical structure, local topology, and atomic feature correlations for molecular property prediction. The authors also provide a web server, aiming to improve accuracy and reduce failure rates in drug design.

papers.title: DFRL-Mol: a dual-stage framework of reinforcement learning for multi-scenario molecule optimization.
papers.abstract: As a critical step in drug discovery, molecule optimization aims to improve specific properties of lead compounds. Inspired by isosteres (i.e. molecular substructures with similar reactive electron shells), existing AI-based methods have been proposed for molecule optimization. However, they often rely on available matched molecular pairs (MMPs), thus facing two essential challenges. First, the limited diversity of available MMPs leads to biased training and a lack of novelty in the optimized molecules, in both single-objective (SO) and multi-objective (MO) optimization. Second, the low number
papers.summary: DFRL-Mol introduces a dual-stage reinforcement learning framework for molecule optimization that overcomes the reliance on limited matched molecular pairs (MMPs) used by prior AI methods. By addressing biased training and low novelty in both single- and multi-objective optimization, the approach aims to generate more diverse and novel optimized molecules for drug discovery.

papers.title: Expanding Quantitative Medicines' Reach: Systems and Methods to Enhance R&D Productivity and Decision-Making in the Agentic-Era.
papers.abstract: Despite integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into drug discovery and an expanding global medicines pipeline, new drug approvals have declined, highlighting a paradox in biopharma: More drugs discovered, but less approvals, higher costs, and longer timelines. Reasons for the decreased research and development (R&D) efficiency are multifactorial, in part driven by the complexity of new modalities, difficult targets and indications, and persistence of cognitive biases in clinical decision-making. One proposed solution to address R&D productivity challenges includes the adoption of organiza
papers.summary: This perspective examines the paradox in biopharma where AI-driven drug discovery has expanded the pipeline yet new drug approvals have declined amid rising costs and longer timelines. The authors argue that R&D inefficiency stems from complex new modalities, difficult targets, and persistent cognitive biases in clinical decision-making, and propose organizational and systems-level approaches—including agentic AI—to improve productivity and decision quality.

papers.title: Decoupling topological and molecular features for interpretable biomolecular interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biomolecular interactions is fundamental to understanding cellular mechanisms and advancing drug discovery. However, biomolecular interactions exhibit immense diversity across multiple dimensions. Most existing computational methods are designed to handle one specific task or data modality, which limits their applicability and generalization capability in broader scenarios. To address this methodological rigidity, we propose a flexible framework for multi-modal feature fusion in biomolecular interaction prediction (FlexBIP). The core of FlexBIP lies in its modular architecture, whic
papers.summary: FlexBIP is a modular framework that predicts biomolecular interactions by fusing multi-modal features while decoupling topological and molecular representations, allowing it to handle diverse interaction types and data modalities within a single architecture. This flexibility addresses the rigidity of existing task- or modality-specific methods, potentially improving generalization across drug discovery and cellular mechanism studies.

papers.title: Comprehensive evaluation of AlphaFold/OpenFold prediction of experimentally unresolved proteins through novel metrics.
papers.abstract: Predicting accurate protein structures is essential for understanding molecular mechanisms, interpreting the impact of sequence variation, and supporting translational applications ranging from drug discovery to clinical genomics. Recent advances in deep-learning-based predictors such as AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 have transformed structural biology, enabling routine in silico modeling even for challenging or previously uncharacterized proteins. However, systematic benchmarking of these tools-especially for novel targets and single amino acid variants-remains limited. Conventional gl
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 on experimentally unresolved proteins and single amino acid variants using novel evaluation metrics. It reveals how these deep-learning structure predictors perform on challenging targets where no experimental ground truth exists, highlighting strengths and limitations for variant effect prediction.

papers.title: Integrative In Silico Profiling of Major Phytochemicals From a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum Mixture: Docking, Molecular Dynamics, ADMET, and Ligand-Based Target Prediction on Shared Pathways in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) converge through metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and impaired neuronal signaling, providing a rationale for multi-target intervention. This study aimed to identify phytochemicals from a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum mixture that may modulate this disease axis. Seven constituents were screened against AChE, BACE1, DPP4, glucokinase, GSK3β, and TACE using molecular docking and MM-GBSA rescoring. Prioritized complexes underwent triplicate 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, post-MD MM-GBSA analysis, physicoch
papers.summary: This study used computational docking, molecular dynamics, and ADMET profiling to screen seven phytochemicals from a three-plant mixture against six protein targets shared between type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. The work identifies candidate compounds that may modulate both metabolic and neurodegenerative pathways, though findings remain purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: KGTC-DDA is a computational framework that predicts drug-disease associations by combining parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks connected via cross-attention. This hybrid design aims to capture both local structural patterns in the drug-disease knowledge graph and global dependencies, improving drug repurposing predictions over existing similarity-plus-GNN approaches.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a RoBERTa-based framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to predict molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This transformer approach aims to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by providing a scalable and cost-effective alternative to experimental binding assays.

papers.title: Combining Phytochemical and Computational Approach on Citrus hystrix DC. (Kaffir Lime) Peel Extract: Anti-Diabetic and Anti-Inflammatory Activities.
papers.abstract: The peel of Citrus hystrix DC. (kaffir lime), an underexploited agro-industrial by-product, may have bioactives. This work tested the ethanolic extract of C. hystrix peel's (EeChP) phytochemicals by GC-MS profiling, and the antidiabetic effect was evaluated using the alpha-amylase inhibitory test, and the anti-inflammatory activity was done using the human red blood cell (HRBC) membrane model. The antibacterial effect was determined using the agar well diffusion method against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. Major constituents subjected to pharmacokinetic and ADMET filtering, molec
papers.summary: This study profiles the phytochemicals in kaffir lime peel extract using GC-MS and tests its antidiabetic, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial activities in vitro. The extract showed alpha-amylase inhibition and anti-inflammatory effects in the HRBC membrane model, with major compounds subjected to ADMET and molecular docking analyses. The work suggests kaffir lime peel, an agro-industrial by-product, may have bioactive potential worth further investigation.

papers.title: Novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus: Distribution in reproductive organs and integrated biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: While the chemical constituents of flower buds from several Panax species have been reported, the phytochemical profile of the flower buds of Vietnamese ginseng remains understudied, particularly alkaloids. This study aimed to characterize alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus (PVF), investigate their distribution across reproductive plant parts, and their biological relevance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus, a previously understudied Vietnamese ginseng variety. The authors map the distribution of these alkaloids across reproductive organs and evaluate their biological activities, expanding the known phytochemical profile of Panax species.

papers.title: GC-MS-Based Phytochemical Profiling and Integrated Evaluation of Antioxidant, Antibacterial, and In Silico Studies of Kumaun Himalayan Strobilanthes Species.
papers.abstract: Five Strobilanthes species indigenous to the Kumaun Himalayan region of Uttarakhand, India, have been historically employed in traditional medicine to treat bacterial infections, inflammatory conditions, and respiratory ailments, but remain largely unexplored for aquaculture disease management applications. Dichloromethane extracts of S. glutinosa (SGDE), S. pentastemonoides (SPDE), S. angustifrons (SADE), S. attenuata (SATDE) and S. tomentosa (STDE) were comprehensively analysed by GC-MS for phytochemical profiling, with antioxidant activity quantified using DPPH radical scavenging and ferroz
papers.summary: This study used GC-MS to profile the phytochemical composition of dichloromethane extracts from five Strobilanthes species native to the Kumaun Himalaya, then evaluated their antioxidant and antibacterial activities alongside in silico (computational) analyses. The work represents an initial chemical and bioactivity characterization of these traditionally used but understudied medicinal plants, with a stated interest in potential aquaculture disease management applications.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides.
papers.abstract: Identifying interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13)-inducing peptides is important for drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening is costly and time-consuming. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed that distinguish functional peptides from no-function ones, but their performance is limited by the small number of experimentally validated peptides. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation framework, GDA, and its prediction system, GDA-Pred, to improve the performance of stat
papers.summary: The authors present GDA-Pred, a framework that uses generative AI to create synthetic peptide data to augment the small number of experimentally validated IL-6 and IL-13-inducing peptides. This data augmentation improves the performance of machine learning models for predicting immunomodulatory peptides, which could aid drug discovery in cancer and immune disorders.

papers.title: The Dual Face of Gingival Mesenchymal Stem Cell Paracrine Signalling in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Pro-Tumour Transcriptional Programme and a Hypothesis-Generating Drug-Repurposing Screen.
papers.abstract: Background: In our companion study, the gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) secretome suppresses oxidative stress and induces apoptosis in primary oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, where those wet-lab results are themselves reported as preliminary; here we ask whether it also engages a proliferation × migration programme in patient tissue. The two arms differ in read-out type (apoptosis and redox there, transcript abundance here), not in opposed function. Methods: Primary OSCC cells received GMSC-conditioned medium (GMSC-CM) or indirect Transwell co-culture, assayed by RT-qPCR (VEGF
papers.summary: This study examines how paracrine signals from gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) affect oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, finding a pro-tumour transcriptional programme involving proliferation and migration genes in patient tissue. The authors also perform a hypothesis-generating drug-repurposing screen based on these transcriptional signatures. The work contrasts with a companion study showing GMSC secretome suppresses oxidative stress and induces apoptosis, highlighting context-dependent dual effects.

papers.title: Molecular Docking and Prediction of ADMET/Drug-Likeness Properties of Potential Bioactive Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Compounds Isolated From the Essential Oil of Capparis Spinosa L. Leaves.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease and one of the most prevalent complex inflammatory disorders. Capparis spinosa L. (C. spinosa) is recognized for its diverse medicinal properties. Traditionally, the plant has been employed to alleviateconditions such as paralysis, gastrointestinal infections, rheumatism, diabetes, anemia, pain, and eye infections. This study aimed to investigate the potential interactions and predicted pharmacological relevance of major compounds identified in the essential oil of C. spinosa leaves using computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and ADMET/drug-likeness prediction to evaluate major compounds from Capparis spinosa leaf essential oil as potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis agents. The computational analysis suggests these natural compounds may interact with RA-related targets and possess favorable pharmacological profiles, though experimental validation is lacking.

papers.title: Polyphenol-Rich Opuntia ficus-indica Cladodes: An Integrated Metabolomic, In Vivo and In Silico Study Supporting Their Hypolipidemic and Hepatoprotective Effects.
papers.abstract: Background: Hyperlipidemia is a major risk factor for cardiometabolic disorders, including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and is closely associated with oxidative stress. Opuntia ficus-indica (OFI) cladodes are recognized as a rich source of bioactive phytochemicals; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their metabolic benefits remain incompletely understood. Objectives: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective potential of a polyphenol-rich O. ficus-indica cladode extract (OCE) using an integrated approach combining in vivo evalua
papers.summary: This study combined metabolomic profiling, in vivo animal experiments, and in silico modeling to investigate how a polyphenol-rich extract from Opuntia ficus-indica (prickly pear) cladodes affects hyperlipidemia and liver health. The extract showed hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective effects, with the integrated approach helping to clarify the molecular mechanisms behind these metabolic benefits.

papers.title: Three privileged scaffolds, one pipeline: chalcones, pyrazolines and pyrazoles in drug discovery and fluorescent sensing.
papers.abstract: Chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles constitute a uniquely powerful discovery pipeline in which each is a privileged scaffold with distinct applications, while also serving as the synthetic precursor to the next. Despite a theoretical chalcone library exceeding 680 000 unique structures accessible from commercial starting materials alone, fewer than 5140 examples have been reported in the literature-representing just 0.8% of this chemical space. Combining this precursor library with the downstream pyrazoline and pyrazole chemical spaces yields a combined landscape conservatively estimated to
papers.summary: This review highlights chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles as privileged scaffolds in drug discovery and fluorescent sensing, noting that they form a sequential synthetic pipeline where each serves as a precursor to the next. The authors estimate that over 680,000 chalcone structures are theoretically accessible from commercial starting materials, yet only 0.8% have been reported, revealing a vast underexplored chemical space. The paper likely surveys synthetic routes, biological activities, and sensing applications while advocating for broader exploration of these scaffolds.

papers.title: Uncharted phytochemical frontiers: a systematic review of novel bioactive compounds from underexplored aromatic plants for cancer therapy.
papers.abstract: Cancer continues to cause a high degree of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making it essential for new, safer, and more effective therapies to be developed. Aromatic plants provide researchers with diverse secondary metabolites that may have useful pharmacological effects. This systematic review examines several aromatic plants that were used medicinally in the past but have not been examined recently for their potential to produce new bioactive molecules with anticancer activity.
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys underexplored aromatic plants as sources of novel bioactive compounds with potential anticancer activity. It highlights secondary metabolites from traditionally used but scientifically neglected species as promising leads for new cancer therapies. The work is a synthesis of existing literature rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in rheumatoid arthritis: current applications and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a highly prevalent systemic autoimmune disease characterized by a complex and partially understood pathogenesis. The substantial challenges in early identification and marked therapeutic heterogeneity pose a significant burden on affected patients. Despite notable advancements in diagnostic techniques and therapeutic interventions in recent years, optimal patient care remains hindered by several ongoing clinical challenges. To address these limitations, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into the field of rheumatology. By leveraging its p
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to rheumatoid arthritis, covering current uses and future directions. It highlights AI's potential to address challenges in early diagnosis and treatment heterogeneity in RA, though the abstract is truncated and specific findings are limited.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of AI innovations for tackling antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global public health concern, rendering available antimicrobials ineffective and leading to infections that are difficult to treat. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied across the AMR continuum, including resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, new antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, antimicrobial surveillance, and clinical decision support. In this review, we aim to highlight recent developments in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In addition, we review computatio
papers.summary: This review surveys recent applications of artificial intelligence across the antimicrobial resistance landscape, covering resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, novel antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, surveillance, and clinical decision support. It synthesizes how computational and machine learning approaches are being deployed to combat a major global public health threat.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple dysregulated pathways, and synergistic compound combinations offer distinct therapeutic advantages through multi-target and multi-pathway interactions. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations are inherently synergistic, yet systematically identifying their active anti-aging combinations remains a major challenge. Here, we developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning-based framework integrating molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network embeddings learned via a variational graph auto-encoder (VGA
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework that combines molecular descriptors, ADMET properties, and protein-protein interaction network embeddings (via a variational graph auto-encoder) to identify synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the traditional Chinese medicine formulation Dengzhan Shengmai. The approach aims to systematically uncover multi-target, multi-pathway active combinations that are difficult to find through conventional screening.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis indicates MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients have a clearly increased possibility to develop tuberculosis (TB). However, the common molecular background, useful diagnostic molecules, and treatment-related targets of this comorbidity are still not sufficiently explained. We attempted to search the shared genetic factors and candidate drug targets for RA and TB by an integrated multi-omics way.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify shared molecular features between rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and tuberculosis (TB), two diseases with a known epidemiological link. The analysis highlights MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers and potential drug targets for the comorbidity. The findings suggest common genetic and immunological pathways that could aid in diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Thymol and Limonene as Potent Antimicrobials: Bridging In Vitro Efficacy and Molecular Docking Insights.
papers.abstract: Nowadays, antimicrobial resistance has created an urgent need for elaborating effective and novel antibiotic agents. In effect, bioactive compounds derived from plants have attracted great interest due to their biological activities. This work intended to study and compare the antimicrobial effect of thymol and limonene against multiple clinical microorganisms including gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. Molecular docking and bioavailability prediction of thymol and limonene were also performed. The in vitro study was realized via disk diffusion technique
papers.summary: This study compared the antimicrobial activity of two plant-derived compounds, thymol and limonene, against a range of clinical pathogens including gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. Thymol showed stronger antimicrobial effects than limonene in vitro, and molecular docking analyses suggested potential protein targets, supporting its promise as a natural antimicrobial agent.

papers.title: Catechins as antibiofilm agents: molecular insights for virtual screening and in vitro biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Bacterial Biofilms are of great concern because they are the main drivers of antimicrobial resistance. We investigated the potential of catechins against bacterial biofilms using advanced computational and in vitro models.
papers.summary: This study investigates catechins, natural polyphenols found in tea, as potential agents to disrupt bacterial biofilms, which are major contributors to antimicrobial resistance. The authors combine computational virtual screening with in vitro biological assays to identify and evaluate catechin compounds that inhibit biofilm formation. The work provides molecular insights that could guide the development of new antibiofilm therapeutics.

papers.title: Repurposing MK0873 as a non-covalent hTERT-Targeting compound: a proof of concept study.
papers.abstract: Telomerase is a key regulator of both cellular immortality and aging, making it an attractive target for cancer therapy and age associated pathologies. Its clinical exploitation has been limited by structural complexity and challenges in achieving specificity. Recent structural insights into human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) have enabled the identification of selective inhibitors. Here, we repurposed MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously evaluated in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis and COPD, as a non covalent telomerase targeting agent. In silico docking and molecu
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study repurposes MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor already tested in Phase II trials, as a non-covalent inhibitor of human telomerase (hTERT) using in silico docking and molecular dynamics. The work suggests a potential shortcut to telomerase-targeted therapies for cancer and age-related diseases by leveraging an existing clinical-stage drug.

papers.title: Targeting IDH-driven Oncometabolism in glioblastoma: a computational approach for the identification of potential inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor frequently driven by mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1 and IDH2) enzymes, which promote neomorphic synthesis of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) and subsequent metabolic dysfunction. Although these mutations are associated with different clinical outcomes, therapeutic intervention remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, restricted blood-brain barrier permeability, drug efflux mechanisms, and effective DNA repair pathways. Therefore, this study aims to identify selective inhibitors of mutant IDH pro
papers.summary: This study uses computational drug discovery methods to identify potential selective inhibitors targeting mutant IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes, which drive glioblastoma through production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate. The work addresses the challenge of treating IDH-mutant glioblastoma by screening for compounds that could overcome barriers like blood-brain barrier permeability and drug efflux.

papers.title: Elucidating adverse drug reactions and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin through pharmacovigilance and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: The comprehensive safety profile and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin-associated adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remain to be fully elucidated.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study combines pharmacovigilance data with multi-omics analysis to characterize adverse drug reactions associated with ivermectin and to uncover the molecular mechanisms behind them. It aims to provide a more comprehensive safety profile for the drug by linking clinical ADR reports to biological pathways.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated computational and experimental approaches to show that naringenin, a natural flavonoid, can simultaneously inhibit RAGE-NF-κB signaling and interfere with Aβ fibrillization, suggesting a dual-target mechanism for Alzheimer's disease. The findings highlight naringenin as a potential multi-target therapeutic candidate with better BBB penetration and lower toxicity than current options.

papers.title: Comparative and Subtractive Genomics Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains for Novel Target Identification and Drug Repurposing Strategies.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae has created a major global health challenge due to the limited availability of conserved therapeutic targets effective across diverse resistant strains. In this study, an integrative computational target-discovery and drug-repurposing framework was applied to six clinically relevant K. pneumoniae strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 3012 conserved genes, which were subsequently filtered to nine essential, non-host homologous proteins. Among these, three conserved cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prior
papers.summary: This study used comparative and subtractive genomics to identify conserved drug targets across six multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, narrowing 3012 conserved genes down to nine essential, non-host-homologous proteins. Three cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prioritized as promising targets, and the authors applied drug repurposing strategies to find existing compounds that could inhibit them. The work provides a computational framework for finding new therapeutic options against antibiotic-resistant infections.

papers.title: Sesamum indicum-derived valdiate as a novel neuroprotective agent targeting PDE10A2 and SIRT1 in Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease is prevalent globally, with approximately 4.88 cases per 100,000 people, based on a systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies published between 2010 and 2022. Despite its significant prevalence, no proper treatment is available that directly addresses Huntington's disease. The existing treatments focus on symptom management, such as controlling chorea and psychiatric symptoms. The drugs used for this purpose may also cause side effects, including depression and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies a compound derived from Sesamum indicum (sesame) as a potential neuroprotective agent for Huntington's disease, acting through the targets PDE10A2 and SIRT1. Using bioinformatics approaches, the authors propose this natural compound as a novel therapeutic candidate that could address the lack of disease-modifying treatments for Huntington's disease.

papers.title: Fighting the invader: strategies against intracellular bacteria.
papers.abstract: Intracellular pathogenic bacteria are often-overlooked agent of chronic, recurrent and difficult-to-treat infections in a context of escalating antimicrobial resistance. By hiding within professional and non-professional phagocytes, adopting dormant or slow-replicative states and rewiring host pathways, these pathogens successfully evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotic therapy, thus contributing to treatment failure and, potentially, carcinogenesis. Here we synthesise how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, and interpret these
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade host cells, persist in dormant or slow-replicating states, and evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotics. It highlights these pathogens as underappreciated causes of chronic, recurrent, hard-to-treat infections amid rising antimicrobial resistance, and discusses strategies to counter them.

papers.title: Computational blueprint and stereochemical validation of a small peptide derived from Lacticaseibacillus casei VITCM05 targeting estrogen receptor alpha and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, necessitating the development of safer and more targeted therapeutic strategies. This study computationally extends our previous experimental investigation of a peptide derived from Lacticaseibacillus casei by evaluating its interactions with two clinically relevant breast cancer targets, estrogen receptor alpha (ERα; PDB ID: 3ERT) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2; PDB ID: 1N8Z).
papers.summary: This study computationally models how a small peptide from the probiotic bacterium Lacticaseibacillus casei binds to two breast cancer drug targets, estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and HER2. Using molecular docking and stereochemical validation, the authors propose that the peptide could interact with both receptors, extending their earlier experimental work toward a potential targeted therapeutic.
